title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
gist: Kiloamp currents at sub-1V in AI accelerators make lateral power delivery untenable (Intel Foundry: resistive losses rise from 8% to 31% going from 1kW to 5kW GPUs), driving voltage regulation into the PCB backside, package and interposer via IVRs, backside PDNs and dense passives; the shift is fueling M&A (ADI-Empower, onsemi-Ferric up to $775M) and expanding OSAT and EDA roles in PDN co-design.

insights.claim: AI/HPC chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU push current to 1,000 A and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop; multi-chiplet designs further increase current density, making power delivery a significant performance limiter.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Power delivery is now a gating spec for AI accelerators — a growing content opportunity for power semis and packaging.
insights.locator: Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter

insights.claim: Per an Intel Foundry illustration, scaling from a 1kW to a 5kW GPU with motherboard voltage regulators keeps VR losses ~13% but raises resistive losses from 8% to 31% and voltage droop from 17% to 31%.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Lateral power delivery is untenable at multi-kW accelerators, forcing vertical/integrated power architectures.
insights.quote: While losses from the voltage regulator itself stay constant at around 13%, resistive losses jump from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rises from 17% to 31%.
insights.locator: A simple illustration shows how the power efficiency drops

insights.claim: At kiloampere currents even milliohm-level PDN resistance causes significant IR drop that directly erodes maximum operating frequency and Vmin, and fast workload transients force voltage guardbands that waste further power.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Better PDN = higher Fmax/lower power — directly monetizable performance for accelerator vendors.
insights.quote: “AI accelerators are now operating at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the power-delivery network can result in significant IR drop.

insights.claim: TSMC says energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Foundry roadmap priorities are pivoting to perf-per-watt, favoring power-delivery innovation.
insights.quote: “Energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward,”
insights.locator: Reconfiguring the PDN is part of a much larger drive

themes.theme: Vertical, integrated and fully integrated delivery

insights.claim: The roadmap moves voltage regulators progressively closer to the load: under the PCB (vertical power delivery), inside the processor package below the SoC (integrated), and into the interposer itself (fully integrated power delivery).
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Each step shifts power content from board-level VRM suppliers toward package/interposer and IVR suppliers.
insights.locator: The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's 18A was the first to bring backside power delivery into leading-edge HVM, and Samsung and TSMC plan backside PDNs at future advanced nodes starting next year.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Backside power is a near-term node differentiator; Intel has a first-mover window.
insights.quote: Intel Foundry’s 18A was the first to move backside wafer processing in leading-edge high-volume manufacturing.

insights.claim: Backside power reduces IR drop and frees frontside routing but does not eliminate power-integrity problems and complicates heat-removal paths, making PI-thermal co-optimization increasingly important.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Thermal and multiphysics simulation demand rises alongside backside PDN adoption.

insights.claim: Next-gen AI data centers are adopting 800V DC distribution stepped down via DC-DC converters (e.g., 48V, 12V, 0.7V), with IVRs at the point of load; fewer conversion stages improve efficiency and cut cooling needs.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: 800V DC is a rack-level power-architecture shift benefiting high-voltage power semis and converter suppliers.
insights.locator: For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands

insights.claim: Moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs cuts IR drop and shortens droop response from milliseconds to microseconds, enabling fine-grained per-region voltage tuning; proteanTecs pairs this with per-cycle on-chip timing-margin monitoring to safely lower voltage.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: On-die monitoring plus IVR control is a power-saving combo; monitoring IP vendors gain relevance.

insights.claim: Analog Devices completed its acquisition of Empower Semiconductor (integrated voltage regulators and silicon capacitors) to expand AI compute power delivery 'from grid to core'.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Analog/power incumbents are buying IVR startups to own point-of-load AI power — consolidation theme.
insights.locator: In July of this year, Analog Devices completed

insights.claim: onsemi announced on Nov. 2 it will acquire the assets of Ferric, an integrated voltage regulator developer using thin-film magnetic inductors, for up to $775 million.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: IVR assets command large valuations; watch remaining independent IVR/power-module players as targets.
insights.locator: In addition, on Nov. 2, onsemi announced

insights.claim: Marvell's Package Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR), introduced June 2025, replaces discrete VR components inches away on the PCB with silicon converters and passives tightly coupled to the processor, with partners Infineon, Ferric, Monolithic Power Systems and Empower.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Marvell's custom-ASIC platform is bundling power delivery; partners' ownership changes (ADI, onsemi) reshape that ecosystem.

insights.claim: ASE's PowerSiP platform for PCB-backside power integration claims parasitic routing-loss reductions of 50% or more by shortening the high-current path.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: OSATs are capturing power-delivery integration content in AI packaging.
insights.quote: “By shortening the high-current transmission path, our solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more, translating directly into meaningful power savings at the system level,”
insights.locator: “Power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Super High Density MIM capacitors improve capacitance density 10x over conventional MIM with potential nanosecond response, developed in collaboration with UMC on 12nm finFET and pitched as integrable across foundries.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Compact passives are becoming a key differentiator in high-density power delivery.
insights.locator: In what Intel Foundry refers to as a Super High Density MIM

insights.claim: Inductors have been the biggest passive bottleneck due to footprint; Intel integrates them into packages using copper-plated through-holes with high-permeability magnetics to limit stray fields.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Magnetic-material and embedded-inductor suppliers are enablers of in-package power.
insights.locator: Inductors have traditionally been one of the greatest passive bottlenecks

insights.claim: IVRs embedded as 3D stacks (deep-trench capacitor, PMIC, inductor) in substrates/interposers reduce parasitics but add thermal, stress and noise-coupling effects on neighboring dies.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: Integration risks create demand for multiphysics signoff tools.
insights.locator: “The IVR is implemented as a 3D stack

insights.claim: Intel's low-voltage GaN MOSHEMT-on-CMOS devices target >12V applications, monolithically integrating GaN power switches with GaN nMOS drivers to cut conversion stages and speed transient response.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: GaN-on-CMOS is a potential path for in-package high-voltage conversion.

themes.theme: OSATs and EDA in PDN co-design

insights.claim: Power integrity can no longer be optimized separately at PCB, substrate, interposer and transistor levels; Amkor says the best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across die, package and board, with OSATs brought in earlier for package-level PDN co-simulation.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: OSATs' role (and content) in AI packaging is expanding into electrical design and validation.
insights.quote: “The best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board.
insights.locator: Kizeev breaks down the supply chain

insights.claim: A Synopsys customer using 3DIC Compiler with RedHawk-SC moved system-level PI analysis into early architecture, cutting iterations from days to hours.
insights.speaker: Laura Peters
insights.so_what: EDA multiphysics/PI tools see rising demand from 3D/chiplet AI designs.
